prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes (Airport Duty Manager=ADM declares; Business Rules Registry holds thresholds/latency/connection protection/gate compatibility/towing priority/stand reopening/turnaround margins/materiality): Normal; Adverse Weather (tighter escalation for near-departure flights; ADM may reduce remote stand use); Capacity Reduction State(extended metering horizon); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit; remote stands absorb late arrivals, contact gates kept for tight/connection-sensitive flights); Contingency Fallback(exception summaries via Contingency Operations Console); Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms). Actors: Regional Flow Manager=RFM(ranks diversions; uses repeated remote stand transfer delays in tactical capacity assessment), Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor, ADM(Medical Diversion Notice; remote stand posture in Foxglove; produces Customs Hold Release Note), Ramp Control Lead(remote stand route/transfer/contingency; uses Towbar Shortage Report), Ground Handling Dispatcher=GHD(produces Towbar Shortage Report; bus conflicts), Aircraft Operator Rep, Airline Operations Coordinator(may request TOBT revision on bus shortage/terminal delay), Slot Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Deicing Coordinator, Meteorology Briefing Officer=MBO, Data Governance Steward. Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform(flight records carry border release readiness attribute, separate from aircraft/commercial readiness). Parts: Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service; CAM=Capacity Assessment Module(persistent remote stand limits reduce gate throughput); Arrival Regulation Console; Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT, GDP, Pushback Window Token); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(Collaborative Decision Log; records remote stand reason, flights, transfer duration, control position); Common Situation Display(time-ordered remote stand status); Emberline=Departure Metering Service(CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager); Ironleaf no advance unless remote stand release supports taxi; Nightjar; Halcyon; Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Apron Sensors; Ramp Movement Board; Gate Conflict Detector(contact gate vs inadequate remote stand); Handling Resource Planner(Remote Stand Shuttle Count); Performance Analytics Warehouse(remote stand timing); Airline Interface Adapter; Sector Load Monitor; Lantern; Alert. Reqs: remote stand departure not ready for push/tow until passengers, bags,

New part:
S570: A flight under a customs hold may remain physically parked and technically serviceable while still being unavailable for normal passenger, baggage, or crew movement decisions.
S571: When border release status is unknown, the Demand Prediction Service treats the turnaround milestone as uncertain rather than assuming that the planned connection interval is valid.
S572: The Airport CDM Portal displays border and customs status in a controlled view so that only authorized operational users see the clearance condition needed for coordination.
S573: The Regional Flow Manager uses aggregated border delay exposure to decide whether an arrival regulation should be adjusted or whether delay absorption should remain local to the airport.
S574: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses customs hold visibility to adjust connection protection, passenger messaging assumptions, and expected aircraft turnaround timing.
S575: The Slot Allocation Engine treats an unresolved customs hold as a reason to avoid assigning an aggressive departure sequence position to the affected flight.
S576: The Arrival Regulation Console uses the Medical Diversion Notice to protect arrival priority, stand assignment timing, and downstream border coordination in the active arrival plan.
S577: Customs status changes are time stamped before they are used in sequencing so that operational decisions are based on the latest authoritative clearance state.
S578: The East Apron Sensor reports stand occupancy transitions, pushback lane blockage durations, and sensor confidence values at a synchronized event time.
S579: West Apron Sensor observations are used to verify whether remote stand areas and service roads are actually available for the traffic pattern shown in the plan.
S580: The Surface Surveillance Adapter normalizes apron sensing data into movement, occupancy, and blockage events that can be correlated with flight milestones.
S581: The Ramp Movement Board presents apron sensor events as operational evidence for stand release, taxi lane availability, and vehicle conflict assessment.
S582: The Gate Conflict Detector uses border status and apron occupancy evidence to distinguish a true gate conflict from a temporary clearance delay.
S583: The Tower Sequence Manager considers confirmed apron blockage when determining whether a departure can be included in the next practical movement sequence.
S584: The Capacity Assessment Module applies persistent apron congestion as a local capacity factor when estimating achievable departure throughput during Normal Operations and Adverse Weather Mode.
S585: The Time Synchronization Service is required because customs status events and apron sensor events must align with Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time decisions.
S586: The Business Rules Registry defines which border and customs states block sequencing, which states require human confirmation, and which states are informational only.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
